The '''2005 World Championship''' was the 10th Star Wars CCG World Championship, run by the [[Players Committee]] at Gen Con in Indianapolis, Indiana.<ref name="awards">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Awards and Hall of Fame], starwarsccg.org; Wayback [https://web.archive.org/web/20230817222457/https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ 17 August 2023]</ref> [[Drew Scott]], the eighth seed of the top 8, defeated [[James Booker]] in the final.<ref name="awards" /><ref name="f75427-1300387">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=1300387#p1300387 Post by Yoshi], "SWCCG Worlds Day 3 Standings History", forum.starwarsccg.org (28 May 2020). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261012152200/https://swccg.com/snapshots/forum/t75427.html#p1300387 Internet Archive]</ref> Scott's published lists are a Day 3 Dark [[Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi / Their Fire Has Gone Out Of The Universe|Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi]] deck and Day 2 [[Bring Him Before Me / Take Your Father's Place|Bring Him Before Me]] and [[Mind What You Have Learned / Save You It Can|Mind What You Have Learned]] decks. The Players Committee's qualifier listing dates the World Championship 20 August 2005, at Gen Con.<ref name="pc-events05" /> A day-by-day schedule and the field size have not been found.

The constructed pool was printed Decipher cards through [[Theed Palace]] plus the original [[Virtual Sets (2002-2009)|Players Committee Virtual Sets]] then legal. The wiki files it under [[Premiere - Original VS6]], from the newest virtual cards in the published lists; a numbered cutoff for the event has not been confirmed.

=== Top 8 bracket ===

As given in a 2020 forum post quoting an earlier player compilation (seeds in brackets).<ref name="f75427-1300387" /> Game differentials were not published.

* Quarterfinals: (8) [[Drew Scott]] def. (1) [[Reid Smith]]; (7) [[Nate Meeker]] def. (2) [[Alden Peterson]]; (6) [[James Booker]] def. (3) [[Jared Lockwood]]; (4) [[Brad Eier]] def. (5) [[Brandon Schele]]
* Semifinals: Drew Scott def. Brad Eier; James Booker def. Nate Meeker
* Final: Drew Scott def. James Booker

== Qualifying ==

The Players Committee's Road to Worlds 2005 ran Regionals from mid-October 2004 to January 2005 (two Day 2 byes each), States and Provincials from April to July 2005 (one bye), Mini-Opens (one bye), Opens and Nationals (two byes), and Last Chance Qualifiers in August (one bye); Worlds itself had two Day 1 heats, and the winner was to receive $1,000. A new rule said that tournament directors could not play in their own qualifier.<ref name="pc-worlds05">[https://web.archive.org/web/20041216041033/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/News/2005worlds.htm The Road to Worlds 2005], swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 16 December 2004.</ref>

The Committee's "SWCCG 2005 Worlds Qualifiers Listing" (last updated 27 June 2005; captured 28 August 2005) lists every Day 2 bye. An asterisk marks a player who "won opportunity to design a virtual card". The listing gives the bye holders, not always the winners: when a winner already held a bye, the bye passed down (at the 2005 Tennessee States, Danny Pack won but already held the Alabama bye, so runner-up [[Micah Wooten]] took it).<ref name="pc-events05" /><ref name="pcf-5728">[https://web.archive.org/web/20050802104132/http://www.swccgpc.com:80/forums/viewtopic.php?t=5728 Tennessee States July 16th....], Micah Wooten and Royce Russell (31 May – 19 July 2005), Player's Committee Forums, swccgpc.com. Internet Archive capture 2 August 2005.</ref>
